name: Cybersecurity Regulation (EU institutions)
impact_assessment: None (proposal states an impact assessment was not necessary)
evidence_rating: thin: self-reported implementation monitoring plus a pre-regulation audit baseline; no independent assessment of outcomes
summary: This regulation sets common cybersecurity rules for the EU's own institutions and agencies and strengthens their response team, CERT-EU. The board overseeing it reports that all 2025 milestones were met and serious incidents fell to 8 in 2025, though threats remain very high and staff numbers fall short. There is no independent assessment yet of whether EU bodies are actually more secure than when auditors found them poorly prepared in 2022.

indicators.objective: No impact assessment: the Commission judged one unnecessary because the rules apply only to EU institutions, bodies and agencies. Indicators below are from the proposal's financial statement (1.4.4); progress is reported annually by the Interinstitutional Cybersecurity Board (IICB)

indicators.indicator: Frameworks and baselines in place; regular maturity assessments and cybersecurity plans in all Union entities
indicators.evidence: IICB 2025 report: Union entities set up risk-management frameworks and completed maturity and risk assessments; all milestones foreseen for 2025 completed on time. Aggregate maturity scores not published.

indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline: significant incidents rose more than tenfold 2018-2021
indicators.evidence: 8 significant incidents confirmed for 2025 as of early November, fewer than in 2024; CERT-EU analysed over 800 malicious activities in depth; threat level 'very high'.

indicators.indicator: Levelling ICT security spending as a share of overall ICT spending
indicators.evidence: No spending share reported; IICB notes an internal assessment that cybersecurity staff would need to rise by about 75% by 2027, which may be hard to achieve.

indicators.indicator: Information sharing and cooperation with ENISA and Member State bodies
indicators.evidence: CERT-EU notified all significant incidents to national counterparts as required; participates in CSIRTs Network.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2022), Cybersecurity of EU institutions, bodies and agencies: Level of preparedness overall not commensurate with the threats, ECA Special Report 05/2022
literature.title: Cybersecurity of EU institutions, bodies and agencies: Level of preparedness overall not commensurate with the threats
literature.headline: Preparedness not commensurate with threats; very different maturity levels across bodies; significant incidents up more than tenfold 2018-2021; recommended binding rules and more resources for CERT-EU
literature.summary_plain: Before the regulation, the EU's auditors found EU bodies poorly and unevenly prepared for cyberattacks and called for binding rules - which this regulation introduced.

literature.citation: Interinstitutional Cybersecurity Board (IICB) (2025), IICB Annual Report 2025 on the implementation of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2023/2841, IICB, adopted 16 December 2025
literature.title: IICB Annual Report 2025 on the implementation of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2023/2841
literature.headline: 2025 milestones met on time; entities completed maturity and risk assessments; 8 significant incidents to early November 2025 (down from 2024); >800 malicious activities analysed; staffing would need to rise ~75% by 2027
literature.summary_plain: The board overseeing the rules reports that EU bodies met their 2025 deadlines and suffered fewer serious incidents, but warns that threats remain very high and staff are short.

literature.authors: CERT-EU (Cybersecurity Service for the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies)
literature.title: Threat Landscape Report 2025: A Year in Review
literature.method: annual threat and incident monitoring under Regulation 2023/2841, including counts of significant incidents reported under Article 21; descriptive
literature.outcomes: significant incidents at Union entities, threat actors, initial access vectors, critical exposures
literature.headline: Significant incidents at EU institutions, bodies and agencies fell from 15 in 2024 to nine in 2025 (seven via vulnerability exploitation), and critical exposures to threat actors fell from 20 to 5, while tracked threat actors rose from 110 to 174; CERT-EU says the cause of the drop is unclear.
literature.summary_plain: The EU's own cyber-response team counts serious cyber incidents hitting EU institutions under the new rules. Serious incidents fell in 2025 compared with 2024, even though more hacker groups were targeting the institutions.
literature.period_geography: 2024-2025; EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
literature.quality: Official incident counts from the Regulation's reporting duty; two years only, small numbers, no attribution of the change to the Regulation.
literature.interested_party: CERT-EU is a body set up under the Regulation
literature.citation: CERT-EU (Cybersecurity Service for the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies) (2026), Threat Landscape Report 2025: A Year in Review, CERT-EU, version 1, 8 April 2026
